subtasks.title: Animate the 404 page
subtasks.goal: Wrap the 404 page's header, error block, and footer in the existing Reveal motion layer with a staggered entrance.
subtasks.seam: Reuse the pre-existing global motion layer — the `Reveal` component (src/components/Reveal.jsx) and the `.reveal` / `.d1`–`.d4` stagger classes in src/index.css, whose `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and `@media print` rules already force the final visible state. Apply via `<Reveal as="header|div|footer" delay={n}>` exactly as App.jsx does; add NO new CSS. Preserve the existing inline styles, copy, layout, and colors — motion only.

subtasks.title: Animate the admin login page
subtasks.goal: Give the login card a reveal/entrance animation on mount, matching the public motion feel.
subtasks.seam: Reuse the global `Reveal` component + `.reveal`/`.d1`–`.d4` classes for the card and its inner rows. If a login-specific motion is added beyond `.reveal` (e.g. card scale/fade), define it in src/admin/LoginPage.css and add matching `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and `@media print` overrides forcing the final visible state, mirroring the fallbacks in src/index.css. Class-based styling only; do not touch shared index.css.

subtasks.title: Animate the admin editor and sidebar
subtasks.goal: Apply a staggered reveal to the admin editor's header, sidebar (DayPicker), and editor panel — including a per-item stagger down the sidebar's day/other rows — without disrupting the two-column layout or interactivity.
subtasks.seam: Reuse the global `Reveal` component + `.reveal` classes to fade/rise the AdminHeader, DayPicker (the sidebar `<aside>`), and editor section on mount. The sidebar has ~10 rows (7 days + 2 labels + Vigilance/Note buttons), more than the 4 `.d1`–`.d4` slots, so stagger its rows with the `Reveal` `delaySeconds` prop by index (e.g. `delaySeconds={i * 0.05}`) rather than the delay classes. Reveal must not break the `adm-layout-grid` grid or `overflow:auto` panels, nor the row `onClick`/hover handlers or `SelectedBar` positioning — wrap contents, not the grid tracks. Any admin-specific keyframes go in src/admin/styles.css with matching `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` + `@media print` overrides mirroring src/index.css; do not touch shared index.css.

open_questions.q: Recipe fit: DEV-36 is a multi-surface presentational task, not a data module. 'module' is the closest enum value (decompose one level into per-surface subtasks against a shared, pre-existing seam). Confirm the split of admin into login vs editor is the right granularity — or fold them into one 'admin' subtask.
